_nota: Inglés de context_sources_read.json (2026-11-15): castellano exacto → inglés, que `i18n.localized` aplica al servir (evidence/context_sources.py); el original no se toca. Se traduce lo que redacta EMMA: por qué se añadió una fuente (`why_added`), qué no se leyó (`not_read`) y para qué la tiene EMMA (`emma_use`). NO se traducen, por ser literales de los documentos del equipo: `listed_as` (el rótulo de la línea de la especificación §17) y el `title` de cada lista (el encabezado del documento), ni lo que va entre «» dentro de un texto. Las claves de estado (`read`, `partial`, `not_read`) no cambian. Traducción automática, sin revisar por una persona; lo vigila tests/test_inventories_en.py.

strings.Se leyó entero el texto del enunciado (r: The whole text of the challenge statement was read (summary, background, objectives and considerations) on 2026-10-31, at the address where the site serves it (/2026/challenges/health-monitoring-software/; the one in §17 still gives «Oops! Page Not Found»). The embedded video («2026 Challenge | Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions») has not been watched; the «Resources» tab says «Resources will be available on Friday, November 13.» and links no resource yet, so the classification of resources that the ideation conversation asks for is left for that date; the «Teams» tab is empty.
strings.Es el reto que EMMA aborda. Sus frases,: It is the challenge that EMMA addresses. Its sentences, one per row and with where EMMA covers them, are in compliance/challenge-coverage.md, kept apart from the team's interpretation; what EMMA does not have (gamification) is stated as «no».
strings.Buscando el enunciado: es la frase ofici: While looking for the challenge statement: it is the official sentence closest to what the challenge asks for that could be read.
strings.Tabla «lo leído de NASA sobre el concurs: Table «lo leído de NASA sobre el concurso» (what was read from NASA about the competition) in compliance/challenge-coverage.md: «monitoring physiological and behavioral health indicators» on long-duration journeys. Now that the challenge statement has been read, it is context, not the source of what the challenge asks for.
strings.Buscando el enunciado: dice cuándo se pu: While looking for the challenge statement: it says when it is published and which rules bind the submission.
strings.Calendario y reglas del concurso en comp: Schedule and rules of the competition in compliance/challenge-coverage.md, as a matter for the team: EMMA decides nothing with them.
strings.Índice de divulgación. No respalda ningú: Outreach index. It supports no parameter: what EMMA cites about health in flight comes from pages with their own reference card.
strings.Portada del repositorio del que salen OS: Front page of the repository that OSD-288 and OSD-569 and the RadLab API come from. Each study that EMMA uses has its own reference card, with its population.
strings.Contexto de Columbus para el público. Lo: Context on Columbus for the general public. What EMMA cites about EPM and Biolab comes from the ESA pages of each facility.
strings.Contexto histórico de un sitio no oficia: Historical context from an unofficial site, written in part before the launch. It supports no data of EMMA.
strings.Marco narrativo de la transferencia a Ti: Narrative frame for the transfer to Earth (knowledge base §12): about architecture, never about clinical equivalence. The concrete example that the ideation conversation puts next to it, the origin of HACCP, goes with its sentence in the entry of the HRP food report.
strings.Se leyó la página del vídeo (título, can: The page of the video was read (title, channel, date, duration and description); the video was not watched and its subtitles were not read. After the video, the ideation conversation writes that NASA sees the ISS as a platform for developing miniaturised, autonomous and self-sufficient medical care, transferable to home care, to remote places and to developing countries, without saying where it takes that from. On 2026-10-26 (eighteenth round, U19) that sentence was searched for with a web search engine and its words («miniaturi», «self-suffic», «developing countr») were searched for in five nasa.gov pages (the station's, its overview, its research and technology, the Research Explorer and the second step towards Mars, «Step 2, Station») and in the three books «International Space Station Benefits for Humanity» (2012, 2016 and 2022): it is in none of them. The closest thing, in the 2022 one, is a miniaturised device for treating wounds that «could expand uses from hospital settings to doctors' offices, patients' homes, and even remote locations worldwide», which is not the same statement. EMMA does not repeat the sentence of the conversation.
strings.Presentación de la estación para el públ: Overview of the station for the general public. It supports no data of EMMA.
strings.La referencia de «renderizar el hígado»: The reference for «renderizar el hígado» (rendering the liver; knowledge base §11.1): the Polaris 3D viewer on a CT scan, with findings that nobody has validated. It supports EMMA not presenting the viewer as a clinical verdict; it does not collect the author's clinical data.
strings.Se leyó el texto de la publicación; el v: The text of the post was read; the video that goes with it was not watched.
strings.Ninguno todavía: una frase sobre un andr: None yet: one sentence about an anatomical android; without the video, no idea is attributed to it.
strings.Contexto de quién organiza en el HRP la: Context on who organises, within the HRP, the human research on the station and in the simulations on Earth. It supports no parameter: CIPHER, the Twins Study and the first step towards Mars, which the front page links, have their own reference cards.
strings.Ninguno en el análisis: cuánto duraron l: None in the analysis: how long NASA's longest flights lasted. The mission profile read it without citing it (data/mission_profiles.json); its figures do not enter the risk.
strings.Se leyó la portada de la documentación (: The front page of the documentation was read (overview, installation and index of services); the pages of each service, among them the JPL Horizons one, were not read in this reading.
strings.No se adopta: de astroquery, EMMA usa so: Not adopted: from astroquery, EMMA uses only astroquery.jplhorizons, for the light time (environment/ephemeris.py), and was using it before this reading. It is not a health backend or a source of biomedical data (CLAUDE.md, known pitfalls).
strings.La figura E.2-1 es una imagen y no se le: Figure E.2-1 is an image and was not read; the text and the two tables of the page, in full.
strings.Dos frases del bloque del IMM en /api/fr: Two sentences of the IMM block in /api/framework: an assumption about the crew (§E.2.2) and a limit of the model (§E.2.3). EMMA does not use its per-mission probabilities or its list of conditions.
strings.Se leyó la portada del repositorio con s: The front page of the repository was read with its README; the code, docs/ and the history were not read in this reading, and what changed between the commit that was read and the one EMMA copied has not been reviewed.
strings.EMMA incorpora código suyo: una copia li: EMMA incorporates code from it: a literal copy in polaris/ (licence AGPL-3.0-or-later, NOTICE), which it enters only through app/polaris. What was copied and from which commit is stated in polaris/ADOPTADO.txt and docs/polaris-divergencias.md; this entry is the front page that was read.
strings.No se adopta: ni hardware ni código. Que: Not adopted: neither hardware nor code. It remains as the local, network-free design reference that the knowledge base keeps (§11.2); the specification (§15) leaves the hardware health node as a postponed decision.
strings.Se leyeron la portada, el resumen ejecut: The cover, the executive summary, the list of gaps and the pages that deal with radiation (5, 16, 19, 28 and 29) were read, and «HACCP» was searched for in the whole PDF; the rest of the report has not been reread.
strings.La frase sobre el origen de HACCP que la: The sentence on the origin of HACCP that the ideation conversation puts next to Stuhlinger's letter as an example of transfer to Earth (page 5 of the PDF): «Similarly, the need to ensure food safety through mission critical, medically limited situations drove the development of the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) system by NASA, U.S. Army Natick Soldier Research, Development & Engineering Center (NSRDEC), and Pillsbury. HACCP has since improved food safety throughout food industry (Heidelbaugh 1966).». It is narrative, like the letter: it supports nothing clinical in EMMA. The report is also used by the food and radiation block of /api/framework.
